what: Kirby is America's largest operator of inland tank barges. Its towboats push barges of petrochemicals, refined products, black oil and agricultural chemicals along the Mississippi river system and the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway. It also distributes and overhauls large diesel engines and power generation equipment.
customers: Petrochemical producers, refiners and commodity traders who need bulk liquids moved cheaply, plus oilfield operators, power generation customers and marine engine owners on the distribution side.
money: Inland and coastal tank barge transport of petrochemicals, refined products and black oil.
Sales, service and overhaul of diesel engines, transmissions and power generation equipment, including backup generators.
moat: Barges are the cheapest way to move bulk liquids, and the Jones Act requires that domestic waterborne cargo travel on US-built, US-crewed vessels, which excludes foreign competition entirely. Building new barges is expensive and the shipyard capacity is limited, so when demand rises, rates rise rather than new supply appearing.
risks: Barge rates are cyclical and depend on petrochemical production volumes, which depend in turn on global demand and on US refinery utilisation.
Debt is about $1.1B against only $78.8M of cash.
Low water on the Mississippi, ice, hurricanes and lock closures all disrupt operations and have become more frequent.
Only seven analysts cover the stock, and the $174.71 average target against a $125.37 price is a sizeable gap on thin coverage.
The distribution segment depends partly on oilfield activity, which follows the oil price.
opportunities: Revenue has grown every year shown, from $2.2B in 2021 to $3.4B in 2025.
Barge supply has shrunk for years as old vessels retired faster than new ones were built, which supports rates.
Data centre demand for backup power generation has become a genuine growth driver in the distribution segment.
Free cash flow of $389.3M exceeds net income of $373.6M, and the shares trade at about 18 times earnings and 9.8 times EV/EBITDA.
watch: Barge utilisation and spot rates. The marine business is two-thirds of the company, and utilisation above ninety percent is what lets Kirby push rates higher at contract renewal.
